# GitHub Issue: [Bug]: browser_tool.py UnicodeDecodeError on Windows with non-UTF-8 locale (e.g. GBK/CJK)

**URL:** https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/new/choose → 选 "🐛 Bug Report"

---

## Title

```
[Bug]: browser_tool.py UnicodeDecodeError on Windows with non-UTF-8 system encoding (GBK/CJK)
```

## Bug Description

`browser_tool.py` reads browser subprocess stdout/stderr temp files with hardcoded `encoding="utf-8"` (lines 2113-2116). On Windows systems with non-UTF-8 default encoding (e.g. Chinese GBK, Japanese Shift-JIS, Korean EUC-KR), process output containing system-encoded characters causes `UnicodeDecodeError`, making `browser_navigate` and other browser tools completely non-functional.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Windows 10/11 with system locale set to Chinese (Simplified) — default encoding is GBK
2. Launch Hermes desktop app
3. Trigger any `browser_navigate` call that produces stderr with non-ASCII characters (e.g. a failed navigation, a URL with Chinese characters, or a Windows system error message in Chinese)
4. The tool fails with `UnicodeDecodeError`

## Expected Behavior

Browser tool should handle non-UTF-8 encoded output gracefully, either by detecting the system encoding or using `errors='replace'` / `errors='surrogateescape'`.

## Actual Behavior

```
browser 'open' exception: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xb2 in position 13: invalid start byte
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "...browser_tool.py", line 2116, in _run_browser_command
    stderr = f.read()
  File "<frozen codecs>", line 322, in decode
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xb2 in position 13: invalid start byte
```

## Affected Component

Tools (`browser_tool.py`)

## Root Cause Analysis

**File:** `tools/browser_tool.py`
**Lines:** 2113-2116

```python
with open(stdout_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    stdout = f.read()
with open(stderr_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    stderr = f.read()
```

The `encoding="utf-8"` is strict by default. On Windows with CJK locale, subprocess output (especially from `start`/`cmd` error messages) is encoded in GBK/CP936. The byte `0xb2` is a valid GBK lead byte but invalid UTF-8, causing the crash.

## Proposed Fix

Add `errors='replace'` (or `errors='surrogateescape'`) to the file reads:

```python
with open(stdout_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
    stdout = f.read()
with open(stderr_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
    stderr = f.read()
```

Alternatively, detect the system encoding:
```python
import locale
encoding = locale.getpreferredencoding() or "utf-8"
with open(stdout_path, "r", encoding=encoding, errors="replace") as f:
    stdout = f.read()
```

## Related Issues

This is the same systemic pattern as:
- **#46099** — MCP client TextReceiveStream uses `errors='strict'` → fails on Windows with UnicodeDecodeError
- **#47393** — fix(cron): don't crash on non-UTF-8/truncated script stdout

All three share the root cause: hardcoded strict UTF-8 decoding on Windows pipe/file I/O with non-UTF-8 system encoding.

## Operating System

Windows 10/11 Pro, system locale: Chinese (Simplified), default encoding: GBK (CP936)

## Debug Report

```
Hermes v0.16.0
```

items.title: feat: Add per-call provider parameter to TTS tool
items.body:
## Description

The TTS tool currently reads the provider from `tts.provider` in config.yaml and offers no way to override it per-call. This means switching between providers requires modifying global config each time.

## Use Case

When generating TTS for different contexts — casual replies, polished ad content, multilingual output — different providers and voices are optimal. Currently there's no clean way for the model to pick the right provider per call without modifying shared state.

## Proposed Solution

Add an optional `provider` parameter to the TTS tool:

```python
def text_to_speech_tool(
    text: str,
    output_path: Optional[str] = None,
    provider: Optional[str] = None,  # NEW
) -> str:
```

When provided, use `provider` instead of `tts.provider` from config. Voice configuration would still come from `tts.<provider>.*` in config.yaml (so the user pre-configures voices per provider), but the provider selection happens at call time.

This keeps the current behavior intact (omit provider → use global default) while enabling per-call overrides.

## Example

```json
{
  "name": "text_to_speech",
  "arguments": {
    "text": "The future is now, old man!",
    "provider": "xai"
  }
}
```

Voice settings for each provider are still configured once in config.yaml under `tts.<provider>.*`.

items.title: [bug] anthropic_messages: tool calls emitted as text (not promoted to tool_use) are dropped, agent loop halts without executing the tool

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Summary

In the `anthropic_messages` transport, `normalize_response()` only promotes a tool call when the provider returns a structured `tool_use` content block. When the model emits the tool-call markup into a **`text` block** instead (i.e. the serving layer did not promote it to `tool_use`), Hermes returns `tool_calls=None` with `finish_reason="stop"`. The agent loop then treats the turn as a final answer and **halts without executing the tool**.

This is the same class of problem the existing VolcEngine workaround in `_repair_tool_call` already defends against ("provider leaked malformed tool data, recover defensively") — but at the response-normalization layer rather than the tool-name layer.

### Where

`agent/transports/anthropic.py` → `AnthropicTransport.normalize_response()`

The method iterates `response.content` and collects `tool_use` blocks into `tool_calls`, but has no fallback for the case where a complete `invoke` block lands in a `text` block. Both the streaming (`stream.get_final_message()`) and non-streaming paths funnel through this single method, so the gap affects both.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `provider: anthropic` (`api_mode=anthropic_messages`).
2. Drive a turn where the model emits a complete tool-call block as plain text (observed intermittently with some Claude builds, e.g. when the namespace prefix on the invoke markup is dropped so the serving layer cannot promote it to `tool_use`).
3. The API returns a single `text` content block with `stop_reason="end_turn"` and **no** `tool_use` block.

### Expected

Hermes recovers the embedded tool call and continues the agent loop (executes the tool).

### Actual

`normalize_response()` produces `tool_calls=None`, `finish_reason="stop"`. The agent loop ends the turn as if the model gave a final answer — the tool is never run. Multi-step / dependency-chained tasks stall silently.

### Proposed fix

Add a defensive salvage path to `normalize_response()`: when there are **zero** structured `tool_calls` but the joined text carries a **complete** invoke block, extract the tool name + parameters, re-promote them to real `ToolCall`s, re-map `finish_reason` to `tool_calls`, and strip the raw markup from the user-visible text.

Safety properties:
- Only fires when structured `tool_calls` is empty — the healthy path pays nothing.
- Only salvages **complete** blocks (closing tag required) — a truncated/streaming tail is left untouched so a partial call is never executed.
- Parameter values are run through `json.loads` so `"61"` → `61`, `"true"` → `True`, mirroring what a structured `tool_use` block would have carried; non-JSON values (paths, shell commands) stay as trimmed strings.
- Genuine final text answers are unaffected (no invoke markup → no change).

A PR implementing this with unit + integration coverage follows.

### Problem or Use Case

# WhatsApp Group Sending with Hermes Skill (Termux) ג€” One-File Guide

This guide contains everything in one copy-paste-friendly file: problem summary, fixes, corrected files, install steps, tests, and GitHub notes.

## Overview

This setup lets Hermes send WhatsApp messages to groups through a custom Hermes skill called `wa-groups`, using an external Node.js script (`send.js`) wrapped by a Bash script (`send-group.sh`) in Termux.

## What Was Broken

1. The `wa-groups` skill existed, but WhatsApp/Hermes did not always load it.
2. The original `SKILL.md` had formatting issues.
3. The wrapper script used a wrong hardcoded path:
   ```bash
   /root/whatsapp-sender/send.js
   ```
   which does not exist in Termux.
4. `send.js` expects a full WhatsApp group JID:
   ```text
   <group_id>@g.us
   ```
   not just a numeric group ID.

## Correct Paths in Termux

Hermes skill path:

```bash
~/.hermes/skills/wa-groups/SKILL.md
```

Full Termux path:

```bash
/data/data/com.termux/files/home/.hermes/skills/wa-groups/SKILL.md
```

Wrapper script path:

```bash
~/.hermes/skills/wa-groups/scripts/send-group.sh
```

Node sender path:

```bash
/data/data/com.termux/files/home/whatsapp-sender/send.js
```

Copy this into:


```markdown
description: Send WhatsApp messages to any group via an external Baileys shell wrapper. Use this when a user gives a WhatsApp group number and asks to send a message.
version: 1
---

Use this skill whenever the user asks to send a WhatsApp message to a group and provides a numeric group identifier.

  `~/.hermes/skills/wa-groups/scripts/send-group.sh <group_id> "<message>"`
- The `group_id` is numeric and does not include `@g.us`.
- The script automatically converts the group ID to `<group_id>@g.us` before calling `send.js`.
- Convert every WhatsApp group send request into the shell command above.

# Procedure

1. Extract the `group_id` from the user request.
2. Build the final message text.
3. Run:
```

### Skill appears in CLI but not in WhatsApp

### Bug Description

**Describe the bug**
The desktop app (Electron, remote gateway mode) crashes with
`RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` in the `UserMessage` component
whenever I attach and send a photo in the chat.

After the crash the app is stuck in a crash loop on every restart, because it
auto-loads the session containing the photo and tries to re-render it. The app
only becomes usable again after the session is deleted on the server.

**Likely cause**
The attached image is embedded as a very large base64 data URI in the user
message. Rendering this huge string in UserMessage appears to trigger unbounded
recursion (markdown/syntax processing) and overflows the call stack.

**Environment**
- Desktop client v0.16.0, connected to a self-hosted remote gateway (basic auth)
- Backend v0.16.0
- Affected bundles: both index-mGKaPVL4.js and (after auto-update) index-CqhgUV32.js
- Vision model configured server-side (Gemini) — server side works fine

**To reproduce**
1. Attach a photo in the desktop chat and send it
2. UserMessage render recurses until the stack overflows
3. App crashes and re-crashes on restart until the session is deleted

**Expected behavior**
Image attachments (large base64 data URIs) should render without unbounded
recursion — e.g. render the image element directly instead of passing the data
URI through the text/markdown renderer.

**Workaround**
Delete the offending session on the server: `hermes sessions delete <id>`.
